question.knowledge_point: Identifying Quadric Surfaces by Completing the Square
question.worked_solution:
First, we complete the square in the $x$ and $z$ terms:

$$
\begin{aligned}2{x}^{2}-4{z}^{2}-4x-y-16z-12 & =0 \\ 2({x}^{2}-2x)-4({z}^{2}+4z)-y-12 & =0 \\ 2[(x-1)^{2}-1]-4[(z+2)^{2}-4]-y-12 & =0 \\ 2(x-1)^{2}-2-4(z+2)^{2}+16-y-12 & =0 \\ 2(x-1)^{2}-4(z+2)^{2}-y+2 & =0\end{aligned}
$$

Now, by rearranging, we get the equation

$$
\begin{aligned}2(x-1)^{2}-4(z+2)^{2}-y+2 & =0 \\ 2(x-1)^{2}-4(z+2)^{2} & =y-2\end{aligned}
$$

This is the equation of a hyperbolic paraboloid centered at $(1,2,-2).$
